The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) has cautioned banks, non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) and fintech firms about a growing trend of financially motivated cyberattacks involving artificial intelligence agents.In an advisory issued to financial institutions, I4C, which functions under the Union Ministry of Home Affairs, has asked them to urgently implement the measures prescribed in the advisories issued by the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In).The advisory was issued after the National Cybercrime Threat Analysis Unit of I4C and CERT-In, under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, observed a growing trend of cyber frauds involving cyberattacks on banks, NBFCs and fintech companies.Financial institutions have also been asked to align their security controls with CERT-In’s May 2026 blueprint for reducing exposure and defending against AI-assisted vulnerability exploitation in digital infrastructure, as well as the cybersecurity frameworks prescribed by their respective sectoral regulators.Financial institutions have been urged to report such incidents to CERT-In within six hours of detecting them. Banks and NBFCs are also required to report incidents to the Reserve Bank of India through its DAKSH portal within the same timeframe.

. India’s services sector growth rose to a four-month high in October, boosted by new business and resilient domestic demand. The seasonally adjusted HSBC India Services Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) rose to 55.8 during the last month from 55.2 in September.According to the latest data compiled by S&P Global, new client additions and successful advertising supported the increase in activity, with sales recording their fastest growth since June. Domestic demand remained the main driver of sales growth during October. The report noted that all four broad service categories covered by the survey recorded faster growth in new business and output, with Finance and Insurance leading the expansion. The report highlighted that easing of cost pressures also provided some relief to service providers. Input prices increased at their slowest pace in over six years, while the rate of increase in prices charged to customers slowed to its weakest level since June.Meanwhile, the HSBC India Composite PMI Output Index increased to 56.2 in October from 55.9 in the previous month, marking the fastest rise in aggregate output in four months.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has said that the deep depression over East central and adjoining Southeast Bay of Bengal has moved southeastwards and intensified into a Deep Depression today. IMD added that the deep depression is very likely to move nearly southwestwards, and intensify further into a cyclonic storm over east central adjoining Southeast Bay of Bengal by early morning tomorrow. It has advised fishermen not to venture into West Central and adjoining Northwest and Southwest Bay of Bengal during the next two days.The Weather Agency has issued an orange colour warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall over Kerala, Mahe, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal tomorrow. Heavy Rainfall is also expected over Coastal Andhra Pradesh during the next two days.The Met Department has predictedthunderstormsaccompanied by lightning and gusty winds over Gangetic West Bengal, Kerala, Mahe, Lakshadweep and Andaman and Nicobar Islands during the next two to three days.For Delhi, the IMD has forecast a clear sky tomorrow. The maximum temperature in the National Capital will be around 31 to 33 degrees Celsius, while the minimum temperature will hover around 15 to 17 degrees Celsius tomorrow.

. Young badminton player Tanvi Patri has created history by becoming the first Indian to reach the women’s badminton final at the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar.Tanvi defeated Japan’s Yuzuno Watanabe 21-14, 11-21, 21-19 in a hard-fought 54-minute semifinal to book her place in the title clash. She had earlier scripted history by becoming the first Indian woman to reach the semifinals, defeating Thailand’s Kungkaew Kakanik.Tanvi is the fourth Indian shuttler to reach the badminton semifinals at the Youth Olympic Games, joining an elite list that includes H. S. Prannoy, Lakshya Sen and Aditya Joshi. Tanvi will now face China’s Yi Xin Zhang in the final today.

. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has simplified foreign exchange reporting rules for service exporters and importers, easing compliance requirements for individuals and small-value transactions.Under the revised regulations, resident individuals exporting services will no longer need to submit a separate Export Declaration Form. Providing payment details to their authorised dealer bank will be sufficient. The same facility will apply to other exporters for inward remittances of up to ten lakh rupees.For imports of services, banks will be required to report transactions in the Import Data Processing and Monitoring System only when the importer is not a resident individual and the invoice or contract value exceeds ten lakh rupees. The amendments, notified on 2nd November, came into effect from 1st October 2026.

. Akashvani will broadcast the recording of the annual Sardar Patel Memorial Lecture, delivered by Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan, tonight at 9:30 PM. The recording will be broadcast across the entire Akashvani network on the occasion of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel’s birth anniversary.Delivering the 67th Sardar Patel Memorial Lecture, Mr Chouhan said that Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel’s vision, determination and leadership laid the foundation for India’s national unity and territorial integrity. He said that Sardar Patel’s efforts to integrate 565 princely states remain a defining chapter in the country’s history. The Minister emphasised that Patel’s vision of a united India continues to inspire the nation through the spirit of ‘Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat’.Mr Chouhan also said that, inspired by Sardar Patel’s firm approach towards national security and his policy of zero tolerance towards terrorism, India has responded decisively to threats from across its borders, including through measures such as surgical strikes.As a tribute to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, who served as independent India’s first Deputy Prime Minister and Information and Broadcasting Minister, Akashvani has been organising the annual Sardar Patel Memorial Lecture since 1955. Over the years, the annual event has served as a rich repository of thoughts, ideas and perspectives on a wide range of subjects. It has also provided an opportunity to gain a deeper understanding of India’s diverse cultural heritage and the various dimensions of its developmental challenges.

. Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment Dr Virendra Kumar today inaugurated the Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 at Dilli Haat, INA in New Delhi this evening. The Mela will provide a dedicated marketing platform to artisans and beneficiaries belonging to Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes, Safai Karamcharis and persons with disabilities to showcase and market their products to a wider audience. Speaking on the occassion, Dr Kumar said the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment has been organising Shilp Samagam Melas since 2022 and more than 1,000 artisans from Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes and Safai Karamcharis have benefited from opportunities to exhibit and market their products.  The Minister said that with approximately 150 stalls for participating male and female artisans to showcase their handicraft and handloom products under Bharat TULIP and Purple Fest, the initiative brings traditional artisans, creative talent and persons with disabilities together on a common platform to encourage wider market access and equal opportunities for participation.  The Mela will remain open to visitors until 15th of this month.

. The Department of Pension and Pensioners’ Welfare will conduct the month-long fifth nation-wide Digital Life Certificate (DLC) campaign across the country from the 1st of next month. Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions Ministry said that this is the biggest-ever DLC Campaign undertaken by the Ministry. Electronics and Information Technology Ministry and UIDAI will provide technical support during this campaign. The Ministry said that the initiative will be adopted with a Whole of Government approach with the objective of reaching pensioners in the remotest corners of the country with focus on Face Authentication Technology. The Ministry said that face Authentication for Digital Life Certificate is a seamless and fast mode for DLC generation which can be used both on Android and Apple devices, making it easy and convenient for elderly Pensioners.The Campaign will be conducted in an Utsav mode by offering a bouquet of services such as Health Check-ups and Aadhaar updation for pensioners. Doorstep services to be provided to pensioners based on their requirement.

. US President Donald Trump has said that Washington will stop providing its annual 4 billion dollars in aid to Israel after the end of 2026, following an agreement with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.In an interview, Trump said Netanyahu had agreed to end the financial assistance, although the US would continue to help Israel if needed. It was not immediately clear what form of aid Trump was referring to. Neither Netanyahu’s office nor Israel’s Foreign Ministry confirmed the reported agreement.Trump cited criticism from Democrats, including Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, over US support for Israel as a reason for ending the annual funding. However, analysts said that ending military assistance could take longer than Trump’s proposed timeline, given the ongoing joint weapons and defence programmes. Thomas Warrick of the Atlantic Council said US military aid was unlikely to end by December 2026 and could instead be phased out during 2027.

. India’s 17-year-old tennis sensation Maaya Rajeshwaran Revathi has become the first Indian woman since Sania Mirza in 2012 to reach the quarter-finals of a WTA Tour-level singles event.Ranked 669th in the world, Maaya defeated Polish qualifier Weronika Falkowska, ranked 277th, 6-4, 6-3 in straight sets in the second round of the Chennai Open. No Indian player had progressed beyond the second round in the previous two editions of the tournament.Maaya’s breakthrough marks India’s return to the quarter-finals of a WTA Tour singles event after nearly 15 years. Sania Mirza last achieved the feat in February 2012, when she reached the quarter-finals of the Pattaya Open. Maaya continued her impressive rise this season by winning her maiden W35 singles title in Lagos, Portugal, in October as a qualifier without dropping a set. She also claimed the doubles title alongside Ukraine’s Yelyzaveta Kotliar.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will interact with members of the Indian contingent that participated in the Asian Para Games 2026 at the Indira Gandhi Sports Complex in New Delhi today. He will also address the gathering on the occasion.India recorded its best-ever performance at the Asian Para Games held in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, with 97 para-athletes winning a total of 114 medals. The medal tally comprised 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze medals.The programme will be attended by medal-winning athletes, coaches, officials of the Paralympic Committee of India and the Indian Olympic Association, representatives of National Sports Federations, and officials of the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports.

. Wall Street ended on a mixed note yesterday. Among the major indices, the Nasdaq Composite gained over 0.8 per cent, and the S&P 500 added 0.4 per cent, snapping their three-session losing streak. The rebound was driven by gains in chip stocks. Conversely, the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.4 per cent.

. Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment Dr Virendra Kumar today launched the ‘Vayo Samman Rashtriya Abhiyan’, a National Intergenerational Bonding Campaign, under the Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana in New Delhi.  The initiative is aimed at strengthening intergenerational solidarity and promoting a society that recognises and values the experience, wisdom and contributions of senior citizens.Addressing the gathering, Dr Kumar described the campaign as the blend of experience and energy, bringing together the experience of senior citizens and the energy of younger generations. He highlighted that country’s population aged sixty years and above is projected to increase from approximately ten crore in the year 2011 to twenty three crore by the year 2036. The Minister said that urbanisation, migration and changing family structures have reduced regular interaction between generations. He added that this has resulted in challenges such as loneliness, limited awareness of welfare schemes and vulnerability to cyber fraud among senior citizens. Dr Kumar said the campaign launched today reinforces the message that the welfare, dignity and inclusion of senior citizens are not merely governmental responsibilities but a shared social commitment. He said that the campaign will reach every village and mohalla through Panchayats, local bodies and educational institutions.

. The Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has proposed amendments to the Drugs Rules, 1945, to provide for the immediate suspension of manufacturing licences for drugs declared Not of Standard Quality (NSQ) on specified critical quality parameters.The proposed amendments seek to enable prompt regulatory intervention upon the detection of substandard medicines, prevent their continued manufacture and distribution, and strengthen compliance mechanisms in the interest of patient safety and public health.The Ministry said that under the existing provisions, suspension or cancellation of a manufacturing licence is preceded by the prescribed regulatory procedure, including the issuance of a show-cause notice. The proposed amendment also provides for mandatory corrective measures before the suspension is revoked. The suspension will continue until the manufacturer undertakes an effective Root Cause Analysis and implements appropriate Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) to the satisfaction of the concerned Licensing Authority.The Ministry said that revocation of the suspension will be permitted only after the requisite corrective and preventive measures have been implemented and duly verified by the Licensing Authority. It added that the amendments are expected to strengthen post-marketing regulatory surveillance, facilitate timely action against substandard medicines, and promote greater accountability among manufacturers and marketers.The draft amendments have been notified for public consultation, and objections and suggestions have been invited from stakeholders and members of the public within 30 days. Objections and suggestions, if any, may be addressed to the Under Secretary (Drugs), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, or sent by email to drugsdiv-mohfw@gov.in.

. US President Donald Trump acknowledged that the eight-month-old war in Iran had heavily impacted the midterm elections. Speaking to reporters at the White House after the election results, Trump conceded that voters were deeply frustrated by surging fuel prices linked to the conflict.Democrats swept the polls, taking control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate. Despite the severe political fallout for the Republican Party, Trump firmly defended his foreign policy agenda, asserting that the military campaign was an absolute necessity. He emphasised that preventing Tehran from acquiring a nuclear weapon remains his long-term priority. He also rejected the notion that the election results amounted to a personal rebuke, noting that he himself was not on the ballot.US Vice-President JD Vance distanced himself from the administration’s military strategy, posting online that “the reason we lost is the war”. Meanwhile, Mike Johnson of Louisiana announced that he would not seek re-election as House Republican leader, setting the stage for an intense intra-party leadership battle.Following the Democratic sweep, global energy markets responded immediately. Brent crude oil futures plunged by more than 8 per cent to below 100 dollars a barrel, their lowest level in nearly a month.Incoming Democratic congressional leaders have pledged a swift legislative agenda focused on lowering the domestic cost of fuel, groceries and healthcare, alongside launching sweeping oversight investigations into the Trump administration’s conduct of the war.

. The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports has launched the ‘Khelo Bharat: From Manufacturing to Podium Finish Quiz’ on the MY Bharat portal today. The quiz aims to raise awareness about the government’s efforts to strengthen country’s sports ecosystem. It also promotes domestic sports goods manufacturing and innovation. The Ministry said that the initiative highlights country’s participation and achievements at the 20th Asian Games 2026 and 5th Asian Para Games 2026, held in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan.The quiz is open to citizens, students, youth, professionals and sports enthusiasts. It will remain open until 20th of this month. The Ministry further stated that the initiative aims to encourage people to learn about  India’s growing sporting ecosystem, from manufacturing and innovation to international sporting excellence.

. The 2nd National SDRF CBRN Competition 2026 concluded today at the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) ground in Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh.Speaking at the event, NDRF Director General Piyush Anand said that the NDRF had launched the initiative two years ago to strengthen the capabilities of State Disaster Response Forces.He said the initiative was launched following directions from Union Home Minister Amit Shah to enhance the training and capabilities of SDRF personnel. Mr Anand added that a total of 19 teams participated in the competition.

. In Badminton, India’s Anmol Kharb and Tanvi Sharma have advanced to the second round of Women’s Singles at the Korea Open Super 500 tournament. Anmol defeated Canada’s Rachel Chan 21-19, 21-18 in the opening round. She will next face Japan’s second seed Akane Yamaguchi.Tanvi also registered a hard-fought victory, defeating Japan’s Manami Suizu 21-16, 12-21, 21-17. However, India’s HS Prannoy bowed out of the men’s singles competition after losing 15-21, 21-23 to South Korea’s Yoo Tae-bin. She will face Japan’s Hina Akechi in the next round.In Mixed Doubles, the Indian pair of Dhruv and Maneesha also suffered a narrow defeat, going down 22-20, 12-21, 22-24 to China’s seventh-seeded pair Zhu Yijun and Li Qian.

. Indian Railways has geared up to manage the ongoing festive season rush of Diwali and Chhath Puja, with extensive crowd management preparations underway at several railway stations. Ministry of Railways said that Indian Railways is developing dedicated passenger holding areas, known as Yatri Suvidha Kendras, at major railway stations across the country. This is being done to streamline passenger movement and ease congestion during periods of heavy footfall, including the festive season. The Yatri Suvidha Kendras, or Passenger Holding Areas, are being developed to provide dedicated space for unticketed and waiting passengers. Our correspondent reports that the facilities have been designed to ensure orderly passenger movement and provide a comfortable waiting environment.The holding areas have been designed to accommodate passengers before they proceed to the platform area. Talking to Akashvani News, Northern Railway CPRO  said that at New Delhi Railway station, a holding area is available for both reserved and unreserved classes. He said additional RPF personnel have also been deployed at Railway stations to facilitate passengers.At Anand Vihar Terminal, the Yatri Suvidha Kendra has 14 ticket counters, 16 CCTV cameras, four electronic display boards and seating for 20 passengers. The facility also has separate toilet facilities for male and female passengers, a Divyangjan toilet, an RO plant, 11 HVLS fans and a public announcement system. The aim is to reduce congestion on platforms, in circulating areas and at station approaches by providing designated spaces for waiting and ticketing.

. India has announced an extension of a 500-million-dollar line of credit for road, health and defence projects in Guyana, as External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar met Guyanese President Mohamed Irfaan Ali in Antigua and Barbuda.The two leaders discussed ways to further strengthen cooperation in areas of mutual interest, including trade and investment, energy, agriculture, infrastructure development, digital technology and capacity building.In a social media post, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said India had already completed several development projects in Guyana and that the new line of credit would further strengthen the development partnership between the two countries.The two countries also signed three agreements, including one on the supply and installation of manufacturing projects for Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs), and another on grant assistance for the implementation of Quick Impact Projects.

. Union Culture and Tourism Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat today highlighted that India’s civilizational consciousness will offer valuable guidance in dealing with present day challenges in the country. The Minister stated this at the book launch of Timeless India: Protection and Revival of Indian Cultural Identity under the leadership of the Prime Minister in New Delhi. Mr Shekhawat said that this book offers a unique perspective on the initiatives undertaken by the government to safeguard and revive India’s rich cultural heritage. He emphasised that preserving and revitalising this legacy is essential not only for safeguarding the country’s historical identity but also for shaping its future.This book is written by Former Rajya Sabha Member Tarun Vijay and  published by Indira Gandhi National Centre of Arts and Surbhi publication.

. In hockey, the unbeaten India dominantly sealed its berth in the finals of 9th Hero Asian Hockey Champions by routing South Korea 8-1 and will face Japan tomorrow at the Olympian Balbir Singh Senior International Hockey Stadium in Mohali.Whereas the Malaysian team which lost to Japan by 5-3 in the penalty shoot-out, as both the teams could not score goals against each other during the march time the fist semi-final, will take on South Korea for Bronze.

. The Iranian government today reiterated that Indian vessels are exempt from restrictions imposed on shipping through the strategically important Strait of Hormuz. Iranian lawmaker Ahmad Hayat-Moghaddam, Vice Chairman of the Parliament’s National Security and Foreign Policy Committee said India, China, Iraq and Qatar have been granted exemptions and can navigate the waterway without restrictions.Speaking at a meeting reviewing the country’s economic and security situation, Hayat-Moghaddam said the exemption for India was intended to facilitate the import of essential medicines, while China’s exemption was linked to broader political and economic interests.Meanwhile, senior Iranian political leaders are reportedly urging the country’s military leadership to consider a diplomatic proposal brokered by Qatar, amid growing fears of a renewed military confrontation with the United States. According to media reports, Iran’s internal assessments suggest that a resumption of direct hostilities with Washington is now considered the most likely scenario. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi have reportedly urged the military leadership to engage constructively with a proposal put forward by Qatari mediators to end the conflict. The report further states that Qatari envoys recently visited Tehran with a specific mandate to obtain Iran’s official response to the proposed framework, rather than engage in prolonged negotiations.The developments come amid heightened regional tensions, with the Strait of Hormuz remaining a critical flashpoint for global shipping, energy supplies and international trade.

. US Vice-President JD Vance blamed the war with Iran for the Republican Party’s defeat in the 2026 midterm elections, saying that some voters who backed Donald Trump in 2024 had switched their support to the Democrats. In a social media post, Vance said the setback was not due to low voter turnout but to former Trump supporters voting against the Republicans.Meanwhile, Republican Congressman Jim Jordan, a close ally of US President Donald Trump, plans to run for House Republican leader, while House Majority Leader Steve Scalise is also expected to enter the race.Democrats have secured control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate, dealing a major setback to Trump. In an interview with a news channel, Trump congratulated the Democrats, saying that both parties would work together during the final two years of his term.

. Most Asian stock markets ended on a mixed note today. China’s Shanghai Composite surged 2.2 per cent, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng rose 1.7 per cent and South Korea’s Kospi gained over 0.6 per cent. In contrast, Japan’s Nikkei 225 dropped 1.4 per cent, Taiwan’s Taiex fell over 0.8 per cent and Singapore’s Strait Times index dipped marginally.In European markets, Germany’s DAX rose 1.5 per cent, and London’s FTSE 100 gained over 1.1 per cent, when reports last came in.

. Indian Railways has announced 1,265 vacancies for Station Master posts across various Railway Recruitment Boards and zones, opening up new employment opportunities for graduate candidates. The Railways Ministry said that in an important recruitment-related decision, the Railway Board has prescribed that Station Master recruitment will be notified separately from 2026 onwards. The dedicated recruitment process provides candidates with a specific notification covering eligibility requirements, examination procedures and vacancy distribution for the post. The online application window will remain open till 25th of next month. Candidates are advised to review the detailed eligibility conditions, vacancy distribution and application instructions before submitting their forms. The recruitment reflects Indian Railways’ continued efforts to provide career opportunities to eligible candidates while strengthening its operational workforce.

. The India Meteorological Centre (IMD) has said that a well marked low pressure area over Eastcentral and adjoining Southeast Bay of Bengal persisted over the region today.It is most likely to persist over the region and intensify into a depression today. It is very likely to move west-northwestwards and intensify further into a deep depression tomorrow and into a cyclonic storm over the Westcentral Bay of Bengal by Monday morning.Under the influence of likely formation of cyclonic storm over the Westcentral Bay of Bengal by Monday and its further intensification, isolated extremely heavy rainfall is expected  over Coastal Andhra Pradesh on Tuesday and Wednesday and  further over Odisha and Telangana on Wednesday.IMD has issued red colour warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall with isolated extremely heavy rainfall over Kerala, Mahe, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal tomorrow.The Met Department has forecast Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep and South Interior Karnataka will experience heavy rainfall tomorrow. The weather agency has said that thunderstorms accompanied with lightning and gusty winds is likely over East Madhya Pradesh, and Andhra Pradesh tomorrow.

. Delhi Environment Minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa has claimed that more than 580 stubble-burning incidents were recorded in Punjab in a single day on the 3rd of this month.During his visit to the Integrated Command and Control Centre (ICCC) at Shastri Park in the national capital, Mr Sirsa said Delhi’s AQI was 60 on the 30th of last month, rising to 117 on the 31st. He questioned what had happened in just three days to cause the sudden rise in pollution, asserting that there had been no new construction, polluting vehicles or industries in Delhi.The Minister said that, according to data provided by the Punjab government, 70 per cent of paddy harvesting had been completed. Mr Sirsa accused Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann of lying about the commencement of paddy harvesting in the state.Citing pollution data from Punjab, he claimed that the pollution level in Bathinda was above 1,100, while it was above 1,000 in Talwandi Sabo.

. In the forex market today, the rupee appreciated by 10 paise to close at 94 rupees and 65 paise against the US dollar. The dollar index, which indicates US dollar’s strength against a basket of six other leading currencies, was trading at 101.45 in intra-day trade.

. External Affairs Minister Dr. S. Jaishankar has urged Commonwealth countries to diversify their supply chains through shorter and trusted routes, saying that better connectivity would boost trade and business.Addressing a meeting of business leaders during the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting 2026 in St. John’s, Antigua and Barbuda, he stressed the need for stronger local distribution networks, skill development and capacity building.In a social media post, Dr. Jaishankar said India’s global business community was an asset for the Commonwealth. He also highlighted digital technology as a driver of efficiency, good governance and growth.He called for greater cooperation on climate action through the International Solar Alliance and the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure, stressing the need for local hubs to support humanitarian assistance. The Commonwealth of Nations is a voluntary association of 56 sovereign member states spanning Africa, Asia, the Americas, Europe and the Pacific.

. In hockey, India will take on Japan in the final of the Asian Champions Trophy in Mohali today. The match will begin at 7 PM at the Olympian Balbir Singh Senior International Hockey Stadium.Defending champions India secured their place in the final with a commanding 8-1 victory over South Korea in the semi-final yesterday.Japan earned their place in the final after a hard-fought contest against Malaysia. Following a goalless draw in regulation time, Japan won the penalty shoot-out 5-3. Malaysia will face South Korea in the bronze medal match.

. The government today launched the sixth edition of the National Startup Awards to recognise outstanding startups across the country. The awards recognise not just commercial success but also social impact, sustainability, and scalability. Launching the awards in New Delhi today, DPIIT Secretary Amardeep Singh said that startups can apply under 20 sectoral categories. He said that in addition, there are three special categories for women, students, and the North Eastern region. He added that the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade is at the forefront of driving reforms to promote startups. Mr Singh also emphasised the need for more private initiative to bring more startups in the country. He expressed hope that the awards would further boost the startup ecosystem in the country. The Secretary highlighted that the award covers a wide range of domains including agriculture, fintech, aerospace, health, education, and accessibility, among others. The applications for the award will remain open until 20 November this year.In line with the Government’s vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat and the goal of a five-trillion-dollar economy, Startup India supports startups through initiatives such as startup recognition, tax exemptions, regulatory ease, funding access, and capacity building. Launched in 2016, Startup India has transformed India’s entrepreneurial landscape, fostering innovation and empowering youth, women, students, and first-time founders, particularly from Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities. Over two lakh 25 thousand startups have been recognised by DPIIT so far.

. The Bahamas has joined the International Solar Alliance (ISA) as its 116th member. The Bahamas’ High Commissioner, Peter Nicholas Symonette Jr., handed over the Instrument of Accession to the ISA Framework Agreement to P.S. Gangadhar, Joint Secretary, Economic Diplomacy and Head of Depository. The handover took place on the sidelines of the Ninth Session of the ISA Assembly in New Delhi.

. The European Union has offered Serbia a fresh opportunity to advance its membership bid, saying that talks could progress if a new student-led government strengthens democracy and the rule of law. Serbia’s membership prospects had weakened under former President Aleksandar Vucic, with the EU raising concerns over democratic standards and warning of possible funding cuts.In its annual enlargement report, the European Commission said Montenegro could become the EU’s 28th member in 2028, followed by Albania and Moldova in 2029. Ukraine is unlikely to meet the conditions for membership before 2030.European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said, “Step by step, we are building a more complete, stronger Union.” The Commission also outlined new roadmaps for candidate countries as the bloc seeks to revive its enlargement process after years of stalled negotiations.

. In a major overhaul of the Agnipath scheme, the Union Cabinet has approved a revised framework providing a pathway for the permanent enrolment of all willing Agniveers into the Defence Forces.Briefing the media after the Cabinet meeting, Chief of Defence Staff General N.S. Raja Subramani said the move follows an extensive evaluation by the armed forces, which gave highly positive feedback on the effectiveness, physical fitness and technological adaptability of Agniveers. The decision comes just ahead of the completion of the initial four-year tenure of the first batch of 18,300 Agniveers next month.As originally planned, the top 25 per cent of Agniveers will be offered regular permanent employment immediately after completing their initial four-year tenure, based on merit. The remaining 75 per cent will now be given an additional engagement period of two years, subject to their willingness and recommendations from the armed forces. After completing the additional two-year period, taking their total service to six years, all remaining willing Agniveers will be offered permanent enrolment as regular soldiers, subject to meeting the prescribed selection criteria.The newly introduced two-year extension period will provide increased monthly remuneration, an enhanced Seva Nidhi package and cumulative seniority benefits. The structural reforms effectively remove the mandatory provision for the exit of 75 per cent of Agniveers, ensuring that those who wish to serve permanently and meet the prescribed eligibility criteria have a direct pathway to regular enrolment.

. Global crude oil prices decline today. Brent crude was trading 1.3 per cent down at 102 US dollars and 21 cents per barrel. West Texas Intermediate crude was trading 1.2 per cent lower at 94 US dollars and 95 cents per barrel, at the time of writing this report.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices were trading around 2 per cent higher in the afternoon session today. The Sensex surged 1,644 points to 78,945, while the Nifty advanced 467 points to 24,428, when reports last came in.On the sectoral front, Auto, Financial Services and Cement emerged as the top gainers. Conversely, Capital Goods, Telecommunication and Media bucked the trend.

. The Confederation of All India Traders (CAIT) has written a letter to Congress leader and Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, expressing the deep anguish and resentment of the trading community across the country over the repeated disruption of commercial activities in Delhi due to political rallies, protests and demonstrations over the past month.According to the letter, CAIT has questioned the Congress rally held on the 1st of this month and the continued support extended by the Congress and other political parties to demonstrations organised by various groups during this period.The confederation said it would await Mr Gandhi’s response to the letter. However, immediately after Diwali, a crucial national-level meeting of traders from Delhi and prominent trade leaders from across the country will be convened in New Delhi to decide the future course of action.CAIT has also announced that a nationwide Day of Condemnation will be observed over the issue. The date for the observance will be decided at the forthcoming national meeting in New Delhi.Speaking to the media, CAIT Secretary General Praveen Khandelwal said the confederation had raised five major questions in its letter to Mr Gandhi, seeking accountability for the losses incurred by traders.

. In the US, the Democratic Party has secured control of both chambers of the Congress in a sweeping victory in the 2026 midterm elections, dealing a major political setback to President Donald Trump and his Republican Party. In a stunning reversal, Democrats captured the House of Representatives and the Senate, ending Republican control of Congress and setting the stage for a new era of political confrontation in Washington.As per the latest results, Democrats have secured at least 228 seats in the 435-member House of Representatives, comfortably crossing the 218-seat majority mark. In the Senate, they have won 54 seats against 44 for Republicans, with two seats yet to be decided.The Democratic gains include major victories in traditionally Republican strongholds such as Texas, South Carolina, Kansas, Iowa and Ohio, signalling a significant shift in the political landscape.The results signal a strong voter backlash against the Trump administration’s economic and foreign policies. Economic concerns, particularly inflation and rising fuel prices, emerged as major factors behind the Republican setback. The prolonged US-Israeli war with Iran, which has disrupted global energy supplies and pushed up fuel costs, also became a major campaign issue.With control of both chambers, Democrats will have greater powers to scrutinise the Trump administration, launch congressional investigations and block key legislative proposals and presidential nominations. However, President Trump will remain in office, retaining his executive powers and the ability to veto legislation.

. The depression, a remnant of Cyclone Arnab, over south Chhattisgarh and adjoining south Odisha has moved northwards.It is now centred over central Chhattisgarh and adjoining Odisha. The Centre has issued an advisory to all States and Union Territories to strengthen fodder security, pasture development and livestock-supportive infrastructure through convergence under the Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) Act, 2025.The advisory has been jointly issued by the Department of Rural Development and the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying. The initiative adopts a whole-of-government approach to address fodder scarcity, strengthen livestock-related infrastructure and support the livelihoods of rural households, particularly small and marginal farmers and landless families dependent on livestock and dairy activities.It seeks to align rural employment and asset creation with the requirements of the livestock sector while ensuring compliance with the provisions and planning framework of the Act.The advisory identifies 22 relevant works from the list of 375 permissible works under the VB-G RAM G framework. These include interventions relating to fodder cultivation and storage, pasture development, livestock shelters, dairy infrastructure and veterinary health facilities.It also emphasises decentralised, bottom-up and Panchayati Raj Institution-led planning, with fodder development and livestock-supportive infrastructure to be integrated into Viksit Gram Panchayat Plans and aligned with local development priorities approved by the Gram Sabha.The advisory calls upon States and Union Territories to prepare comprehensive State Action Plans for fodder security and livestock infrastructure through convergence among the Departments of Rural Development, Animal Husbandry, Agriculture and other relevant sectors.

Indian-American lawmakers have made a strong mark in the US midterm elections, with four sitting Democratic members re-elected to the House of Representatives and another making her debut in Congress. The elections were held yesterday.Ami Bera, Ro Khanna, Suhas Subramanyam and Pramila Jayapal have secured fresh terms while Pia Dandiya made her debut, strengthening Indian-American representation in the US Congress.Bera has won an eighth term from California, while Khanna and Jayapal have also retained their seats. Subramanyam has secured a second term from Virginia. Meanwhile, Pia Dandiya has won Florida’s 22nd Congressional District with 51.9 per cent of the vote. Elsewhere, Maryland Lieutenant Governor Aruna Miller has won another term. However, Indian-American Republican Vivek Ramaswamy has lost the Ohio gubernatorial race to Democrat Amy Acton. The results underline the growing political influence of the Indian-American community, which numbers more than five million people in the United States.

In Men’s Cricket, India have registered a convincing five-wicket victory over hosts New Zealand in the rain-affected first One-Day International at Auckland, taking a 1-nil lead in the five-match series. Put in to bat first, New Zealand were bowled out by India for 185 runs in 40.2 overs. For the hosts, Tim Seifert top-scored with 38 runs, while Glenn Phillips contributed 30 and Daryl Mitchell made 28. For India, Arshdeep Singh led the bowling attack with four wickets. Gurnoor Brar claimed three wickets, while Anshul Kamboj picked up two.Rain interruptions brought the Duckworth-Lewis-Stern method into play, with a revised target of 143 runs in 32 overs set for India. The visitors made light work of the chase, reaching the target in just 22.4 overs and winning the match by five wickets. The chase was brilliantly anchored by Virat Kohli, who smashed a match-winning 74 off just 51 deliveries. Shubman Gill provided valuable support with 37 runs, while Shreyas Iyer contributed 15. Earlier, India had won the toss and opted to bowl.Kohli also surpassed legendary cricketer Sachin Tendulkar to become the highest run-scorer in ODI chases. His brilliant innings took his total runs while batting to 8,741, moving him past Tendulkar’s 8,720 runs.With this emphatic victory, the visitors will look to carry the winning momentum into the next encounter. The second ODI will be played on Saturday at Wellington.I

India  is making a strong showing at ADIPEC 2026 in Abu Dhabi, with companies representing a wide spectrum of the country’s oil and gas industry, from upstream exploration to downstream operations and allied sectors. The participation reflects India’s growing capabilities across the energy value chain, with a focus on indigenous manufacturing, technology and international partnerships.Indian exhibitors at the event have welcomed the scale of the country’s presence, highlighting the government’s support and the growing emphasis on the Make in India initiative. They say platforms such as ADIPEC provide an important opportunity for Indian companies to showcase their capabilities and connect with global industry players.The exhibition has also drawn participation from sectors that support the oil and gas industry, including steel and pipe manufacturers. Exhibitors point out that pipelines remain critical to energy transportation and infrastructure, making their role particularly significant amid the uncertainties in the current geopolitical environment. They say ADIPEC offers an important platform to showcase their products and engage with the global energy industry.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi will interact with members of the Indian contingent that participated in the Asian Para Games 2026, at the Indira Gandhi Sports Complex in New Delhi tomorrow.  He will also address the gathering on the occasion.India recorded its best-ever performance at the Asian Para Games held in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, with 97 para-athletes winning a total of 114 medals. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has announced setting up a Technical Consultative Committee for Financial Markets which will focus on critical policy and operational matters across money markets and government securities.The eight member Committee will be chaired by the Deputy Governor in charge of the Financial Markets Regulation Department, Mr Rohit Jain. The committee will study issues relating to trading, clearing, settlement, reporting and other market infrastructure, including the associated regulatory and operational frameworks. It will also examine the various issues related to the functioning, efficiency, liquidity and resilience of the money, government securities, foreign exchange and related derivative markets.While suggesting measures to deepen and broaden these markets, the committee has also been tasked to identify domestic and international developments, financial innovations, and emerging risks that may affect Indian financial markets.

. PV Sindhu has qualified for the year-ender BWF World Tour Finals. The World Tour Finals will take place in Hangzhou, China, from December 9-13. This is her sixth career appearance in the World Tour Finals and her first since 2021. She had qualified for 2022 but withdrew due to an injury.Sindhu is the only Indian to have ever won the BWF World Tour Finals and has qualified for the 2026 edition in Hangzhou. Sindhu captured the title in 2018, surrounded by runner-up finishes at the 2017 Super Series Finals and the 2021 World Tour Finals.
